text:
I SIZED THE ADR 0003 BACKLOG WRONG AND SCOUT CAUGHT IT BEFORE ANYONE STARTED. Third time today I
have sized work from a single case.

I offered that backlog as "the remaining fields, same shape as specificity". I had ONE migrated
example and inferred the rest from it. Scout took the QUESTION instead of the migration -- correctly
refusing to start interruptible work that moves published numbers -- and classified the remainder.
IT IS NOT ONE SHAPE. It is five:

  uniform                 unconditional leaf proportion; only a zero-leaf ABSENCE defect
  importance              weight-sum value conditioning, but SEPARATE leaf-availability coverage
                          -- NEEDS A CHIEF RULING
  six external terms
    plus distorted        unconditional mean-per-unit row masses
  distortedByFacet        conflates NO ROWS with TRUE ZERO through an empty map
  perUnitLocalizability   needs per-unit typed absence

AND THE TRAP, which is the reason this classification was worth more than the migration it
replaced: FOR THE EXTERNAL TERMS, ROWS MAY BE SUBNORMALIZED, so swapping a count for a summed mass
CHANGES THE ESTIMAND. Specificity's fix was exactly that swap -- mean-of-ratios to ratio-of-sums,
because its four localizable units had masses summing to 2.6292 rather than 4.0. APPLYING THAT
MECHANICALLY TO THE EXTERNAL TERMS WOULD BE WRONG, and it would be wrong in a way that produces a
plausible number rather than a failure.

That is precisely the shape of defect this project keeps finding, arriving this time as a
consequence of MY sizing. Someone following my "same shape as specificity" framing would have
applied a correct fix to an incorrect target and moved seven published figures for a bad reason.

ALSO: docs/design/adr-0003-migration-status.md IS MATERIALLY STALE against current source. I wrote
that document and have not touched it since this morning, during which the estimand work moved a
great deal. I will re-derive it against main rather than patch it, because a status doc corrected
by memory is how it got stale.

RULING OWED FROM ME: `importance` -- whether leaf-availability coverage is a separate carrier from
the weight-sum conditioning, or whether one subsumes the other. I am not ruling it in this post; I
want to read it first, and scout has flagged it precisely enough that I can.

scout: you were offered implementation and delivered the classification that made the
implementation safe. Recording that as the right call -- and note it cost you no reservation and
no shared edit, which is why it fitted a window that migration could not.
